lines.text: PTW Semi Market Brief, Friday 16 October 2026. Here's what moved the chip world this week.
Memory stocks are still digesting Tuesday's AI scare, but TSMC posted another record quarter, and Applied Materials opened a five-billion-dollar research campus.
Taiwan first. TSMC's third-quarter revenue hit 46.7 billion US dollars, up 50.9 percent. Net income jumped 68.7 percent, and gross margin reached 66.4 percent.
Advanced nodes made up 79 percent of wafer revenue, with 2-nanometre already at 8 percent. The full-year growth guide rises to about 44 percent.
A new 3-nanometre plant in Tainan targets 2028, and Arizona Fab 2 aims for mass production in the third quarter of 2027.
TSMC is also evaluating Texas, and talking with a customer building a Terafab, but any fab must be run by TSMC. No deal yet.
In Korea, Samsung showed V-10 V-NAND, the industry's first with over 400 layers: 58 percent more bit density, and 25 percent less power.
SK Hynix is seeking US approval for more American tools at Dalian, linked to talks on a possible NAND fab in upstate New York.
In the US, Applied Materials opened its 5-billion-dollar EPIC Center in Sunnyvale, with nearly four acres of cleanroom, backed by TSMC, Intel, Samsung, Micron and SK Hynix.
SEMI sees 300-millimetre fab equipment spending of 149 billion dollars this year, up 31 percent, and 227 billion by 2029.
In Europe, GlobalFoundries topped out its 1.1-billion-euro Dresden expansion. And in Malaysia, FIC Global opened a Johor plant for AI optical transceivers.
Japan, China and India were quiet. Record quarters still need wet benches that turn wafers this quarter. If that gap is yours, let's talk.
